title: Concise Machine Learning
byline: Jonathan Richard Shewchuk · UC Berkeley CS 189/289A lecture notes, Spring 2024
note: Lecture notes compiled into one report, one chapter per lecture (no numbered sections); PDF page = printed page + 6. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: Shewchuk’s notes for Berkeley’s undergraduate machine learning course, written with his characteristic geometric pictures and blunt asides. They move from linear classifiers (perceptron, hard- and soft-margin SVMs) through decision theory and Gaussian discriminant analysis (QDA, LDA) to regression (least squares, logistic, ridge, lasso) and the bias–variance decomposition, then decision trees and random forests, kernels, neural networks and CNNs. The unsupervised part covers PCA, the SVD, clustering and high-dimensional geometry, followed by learning theory, boosting and nearest-neighbor methods with k-d trees, and two bonus lectures on spectral graph clustering and latent factor analysis.
